name: Mu2e
notes: No physics results exist yet: every fetched status source describes Mu2e as still under construction/installation, with data collection not yet begun (most recently planned for 2027). This is stated explicitly rather than left to silence, per the correctness rule that an incomplete/no-results state must never be implied by omission.

Sensitivity figures: the Mu2e Technical Design Report gives 2.87×10⁻¹⁷ (the key spec since 2026-10-29); the 2022 status paper (PoS EPS-HEP2021 557) gives 3×10⁻¹⁷ for a staged Run-1+Run-2 plan; the INSPIRE experiment record's description says about 2.5×10⁻¹⁷ (the key spec before 2026-10-29, replaced because only that INSPIRE record stated it). Each is recorded rather than silently picking one.

A documented lineage exists to the cancelled Brookhaven proposal MECO (Muon-to-Electron COnversion); no source describing this lineage was consulted, so it is not recorded here rather than asserted from memory.
external.inspire_experiment (1108209) is sourced from https://inspirehep.net/api/experiments?q=mu2e, confirmed at https://inspirehep.net/experiments/1108209.

2026-09-18 verification: the "25 m long superconducting solenoidal system" key spec was removed — the quoted sentence does not appear in the cited status paper (PoS WIFAI2025 020, INSPIRE 3189846) or its abstract, and no fetched source states the length; the 2027 quote was made verbatim (lower-case). 2026-10-29: the Fermilab news feature of 19 May 2023 does state a length, "An “S”-shaped, 82-foot-long system of superconducting solenoids", so the unique-capabilities text uses it; the quoted sentence of the earlier text is still not in the status paper and was replaced.

2026-10-29 INSPIRE re-sourcing: the "experiment approved" interval (2010-08) still rests only on the INSPIRE experiment record's date_approved field. No source that could be read states it; arXiv:0910.3657 (October 2009) already says Mu2e "has been given relatively high priority by HEPAP and Stage-I Approval from the Fermilab PAC", so 2010-08 cannot be the first approval. The date is kept until a readable source is found (the Mu2e status and proposals pages on mu2e.fnal.gov return HTTP 403). The website link and the INSPIRE experiment id are identifiers and keep their INSPIRE basis.

physics_goals.locator: Driutti for Mu2e, PoS(WIFAI2025)020, abstract; "aluminum nucleus" from section 2; "strictly forbidden in the Standard Model" from section 3
physics_goals.note: Re-sourced 2026-10-29 from the INSPIRE experiment record: the 2026 status paper says the target is aluminum (section 2) and that CLFV is "a process strictly forbidden in the Standard Model" (section 3).
physics_goals.quote: The Mu2e experiment at Fermilab is designed to search for charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV) by looking for the rare, neutrinoless conversion of a muon into an electron in the Coulomb field of a nucleus.
physics_goals.value: Search for charged-lepton-flavor-violating, neutrino-less conversion of a muon to an electron in the field of an aluminum nucleus (μ⁻ N → e⁻ N), a process forbidden in the Standard Model

summary.plain: An experiment being built at Fermilab that will look for a muon turning directly into an electron without any neutrinos -- something the standard laws of particle physics say should never happen. Construction is under way; no data has been taken yet.
summary.technical: Fermilab E973 (Mu2e): searches for coherent, neutrino-less μ⁻ N → e⁻ N conversion in the field of an aluminum nucleus using a pulsed muon beam and an 82-foot (about 25 m) system of superconducting solenoids (production, transport, detector) feeding a straw tracker, a crystal calorimeter and a cosmic-ray veto. Proposed 2008, approved 2010, DOE CD-3 construction approval July 2016; as of the July 2026 status paper the experiment is being assembled at the Fermilab Muon Campus, with initial data collection planned for 2027. No physics results have been produced yet.

unique_capabilities.locator: Fermilab news feature, 19 May 2023, section "A big journey for tiny particles"
unique_capabilities.note: Re-sourced 2026-10-29 (changed text). The earlier text, a "25-metre chain of three superconducting solenoids" with a quote that is not in the cited status paper, rested on the INSPIRE-hosted record of that paper. The Fermilab feature gives the length as 82 feet (82 ft = 25.0 m, a unit conversion) and describes the sorting and focusing (the quote elides the sentence's explanation of what solenoids are); it says "system of superconducting solenoids", not which solenoids the 82 feet cover.
unique_capabilities.quote: An “S”-shaped, 82-foot-long system of superconducting solenoids ... will sort negatively charged muons from positive ones. This system will also transport and focus the muons toward an aluminum target.
unique_capabilities.value: An “S”-shaped, 82-foot-long system of superconducting solenoids that sorts negatively charged muons from positive ones and transports and focuses the muons toward an aluminum target
